Meet your headliner. 👑

VIDA AMORE.

25 años. Léelo otra vez — 25 AÑOS. Vida no llegó al escenario, Vida CONSTRUYÓ el escenario. Antes de que el drag fuera mainstream, antes de que las apps existieran, antes de que la comunidad en el Tri-Cities tuviera un espacio propio — Vida ya estaba ahí, haciendo lo que nadie más quería hacer. 💚✨

Cada show de los últimos 25 años empieza con la misma decisión: dar la cara, brillar, y abrir el camino. Esa decisión es la que le dio forma a Washington's longest running drag show. Y el 20 de junio, esa decisión se celebra.

Música por DJ ShaReal — la banda sonora del legado. 🎧

Conoce a la diva. 💗

ALYANA AMORE.

Hay drag queens. Y luego hay Alyana. La diferencia está en la pose, en cómo entra a un cuarto, en cómo la luz cae sobre ella antes que sobre cualquiera más. Es esa cualidad que no se enseña — se vive, se trabaja, se gana. 🌹✨

Cuando Alyana sube al escenario, el público no aplaude por costumbre — aplaude porque no le queda otra. Glamour, carisma, control absoluto del momento. Es la diva que te recuerda por qué el drag es un arte.

El 20 de junio, viene preparada. Y DJ ShaReal viene con el setlist perfecto para acompañarla. 🎧🔥

📍 Azúcar at Out & About — Pasco WA

¿Lista para Victoria? 💋

VICTORIA AMORE.

La elegancia hecha drag. El rojo no es un color, es una declaración — y Victoria lo lleva como armadura. Cuando sube al escenario, no necesita hablar para que sepas quién es: lo dice la mirada, lo dice la entrada, lo dicen las curvas que se mueven con propósito. 👑🌹

Es la queen que viene de la escuela clásica del drag: presencia, control, y un performance que entiende el silencio tanto como entiende el grito. Cada número de Victoria es una pieza completa — principio, desarrollo, momento.

Y atrás de ella, DJ ShaReal poniéndole el ritmo. Porque Victoria no canta sola — la noche entera la respalda. 🎧

The biggest Latino Pride in Eastern Washington is back 🏳️‍🌈🌽

Mark your calendar, because Saturday June 13 is going to be a whole day and night of celebration. Latino/a Pride is back, and once again it is the largest Latino Pride in all of Eastern Washington, hosted right here by Azúcar at Out & About.

We start outside with a full festival from 4PM until 9PM. Think food, drinks, a beer garden, vendors, and live entertainment all afternoon long, and it is all ages, so bring the whole familia. Our folklórico dancers, our drag performers, our DJ, and our cultural artists will all be taking the stage throughout the evening.

Then at 9PM we open the doors and take the party inside Azúcar. We kick the night off with another full drag show, and after that we keep it going with two rooms running all night. One room will be playing English hip hop and dance music, and the other will be Spanish music from open to close. Two vibes, one building, zero reasons to go home early.

This is our city, our culture, and our community out loud and unapologetic. Come celebrate with us.

Latino/a Pride, presented by Azúcar at Out & About. The largest Latino Pride in Eastern Washington.

327 W Lewis St, Pasco.

Meet your hosts for the night 🌟🏳️‍🌈

Latino/a Pride is being opened and hosted all night long by two of our next generation reinas, Abele Fantasy and Bali, and this is exactly the moment we have been building toward. We love putting the new wave of drag front and center, and these two have absolutely earned the spotlight.

Abele Fantasy first caught our eye at our amateur contest, but do not let the word amateur fool you for a second. She has been performing for years and she is a genuinely talented, polished artist who knows how to command a room. She is local, she is fierce, and she does it all like she has nothing to prove.

Then there is Bali, and honey, you already know. She brings the comedy, the camp, and a Selena tribute that had the whole room screaming the first time she did it. Anyone who caught her at our NextGen show can tell you she was born for this stage.

Put these two together on one mic and you get a whole show inside the show. Come out, tip your hosts well, and support next generation drag the way it deserves.

@abele_fantasy and @tranyliciousss

Twenty years in the making 💃

Valeria Sanchez is the kind of artist you only get to witness if you are paying attention. She trained at the Escuela de Bellas Artes in both Mexican folklórico and flamenco, and she has carried that training onto stages all around the world. Twenty years of dedication to her craft, and she is nowhere near slowing down. On top of performing, she teaches, passing everything she knows on to the next generation of dancers.

At Latino/a Pride she takes the stage as a soloist. When the music starts and that skirt begins to fly, you will understand exactly why people call this an art form. It is power, history, and pure beauty all moving at once, and it is rare to see it this close to home.

Do not look away for a second. You are going to want to remember this one.

Folklórico royalty, right here at home 👢

For the very first time at Azúcar, we get to welcome Ballet Folklórico Cielo de México to our Pride stage. This is a local Tri Cities treasure, a crew of five to ten dancers bringing the traditional dances of northern México to life with the skirts, the boots, and the zapateado that you feel in your chest.

These dancers perform all throughout the year, and their famous annual showcase is honestly one of the most beautiful things you can experience locally. If you have never seen it, put it on your list, because it is the kind of show people talk about for weeks afterward. For now, we are lucky enough to have them at Azúcar, and we could not be more proud to share our stage with them.

They also teach all ages, so if watching them makes you want to learn, they are the ones to find. Come celebrate culture that lives and breathes right here at home.

We begin by honoring our ancestors 🪶

Before the music and the dancing take over, we take a moment to honor where we come from. Tonatiuh Xocoyotzin joins us to bless Latino/a Pride with sacred danza, a form of Mexican Indigenous dance that has been carried through generations. He will be accompanied by a drummer and by our own Samadhi Curandera.

This is so much more than a performance. Tonatiuh will share what these dances mean, why they matter, and how they connect us to our roots, especially on a day when we gather to celebrate being fully and proudly ourselves. There is something powerful about holding space for tradition and queerness in the very same breath, and that is exactly what this moment is about.

Come with an open heart and an open mind, and let yourself actually feel it.

@tonamarezoficial

Come for the queens, stay for the goods 🛍️

The stage is only half the fun. Our Latino/a Pride vendor village is fully stacked, so bring a little cash and an empty tote, because you are absolutely going to want to take something home with you.

The Mad Tatter is our resident tattoo artist, ready to send you home with fresh ink and a story to go with it. Belinda's Bloom brings the flowers and that pop of color every good celebration needs. Mad Art Club shows up as your friendly neighborhood art collective right here in the Tri Cities. Bro and Sister Lemonade is sibling powered and seriously sour, the exact kind of refreshing that hits perfectly on a warm Pride afternoon.

Free Mom Hugs will be there too, offering exactly what the name promises, and if you know, you know just how much that can mean to someone. Siren is on hand for photography, so you walk away with a moment worth framing. Rooted Care Collective is bringing the massage therapists, because even your shoulders deserve a little Pride treatment. And Aub's Banana Bread is rounding it out with bread so good we are choosing to keep most of the jokes to ourselves.

Pull up, support local, and treat yourself a little. You earned it.
